newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma govt says investigating attack on Suu Kyi.
newsitem.headline: Burma govt says investigating attack on Suu Kyi.

text.p: Burma's military government has launched an official investigation into last weekend's attack on democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi's motorcade, senior military officials said on Friday.
The officials told reporters the government has opened the investigation with police to find out who was behind two attacks last Saturday on Suu Kyi's car and other vehicles travelling in her convoy.
Suu Kyi, who emerged uninjured from the attacks which smashed her car windshield, has also filed a report on the incident with the police.
One of the officials said the police has tried to take statements from a senior member of Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) party, Tin Oo, whose windows were also smashed in the attacks.
"The responsible officers from the police station contacted NLD vice-chairman U Tin Oo to get his statement. But he said he was not available then," the official said.
Earlier this week Suu Kyi said she had not heard of any government enquiry on the incident.
Suu Kyi has accused the government of orchestrating the attacks. Officials have denied involvement but diplomats said there was no doubt the government was involved to some extent in the incident.
